copies go through a .migrating file, fsync and SHA256 verification before an atomic rename; a failure keeps the original file and appends to the journal

apply treats the plan as untrusted input: absolute target root, no traversal, source inside the legacy tree, protected program directories, resolved-path same-root and duplicate items are all refused before any copy

limits: Linux was executed locally; the Windows result comes from GitHub Actions run 44076049516 on the same delivery commit (Python 1327 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed) and was not reproduced on a local Windows host. Real Windows DPAPI authentication and a real Windows migration are outside this module.

The audit probe that simulates Windows drive-letter paths on Linux now stops at MIGRATION_PATH_NOT_ABSOLUTE; that is a limitation of simulating Windows path semantics on POSIX, not of the Windows behaviour, which the Windows CI test covers.

The audit probes that reuse the pre-fix dist/ snapshot (27afeaa) now stop at the new commit binding or still print that old artifact's numbers; per-item verification uses the rebuilt candidate and the unit tests instead.

The wheel does not contain node_modules or the offline tests: after installing, run npm ci --ignore-scripts in the package directory when Node features are needed; scripts/dev.py exists only in the source package.

Dependencies are pinned to exact direct versions with a license table; no transitive hash lock was generated because resolving every platform wheel needs network access, so artifact integrity comes from SHA256SUMS and the Node lock file.
Source archives are generated from Git objects, so uncommitted work never enters them and a dirty tracked tree must be committed or stashed before a build.

install-check uses a temporary --system-site-packages virtual environment to resolve runtime dependencies offline; it proves the layout, entry points, self-check and untouched user state, not real campus authentication.

Migration copies files only: it does not replay pending transactions, does not decrypt Windows DPAPI ciphertext on another platform, does not copy consent keys or grants and never deletes or moves the legacy tree.
The THU-TODOS-1 and THU-ACTION-1 outer containers are unchanged; record-level storage work remains with 6.1/8.1.
The module ownership table, batch gate and VERSION_MANIFEST were not edited to avoid conflicts with parallel 6.1/6.2 work; batch integration updates them.
No PR was opened, main was not merged, no tag or Release was created; release-manifest.json states candidate-not-released and published=false.
Byte-for-byte reproducibility was verified for two consecutive Linux builds of the same commit; cross-platform reproducibility is not claimed.
rollback: Restore the 6.3 files to bb1f963 (pyproject.toml, MANIFEST.in, requirements*.txt, setup.py, build_support/, the four scripts, version.py, upgrade.py, doctor.py, paths.py, gateway_client.py, gateway.js, docs, the CI matrix and the two test files). The _bundled directory is additive: removing it returns resource resolution to the source layout. dist/ can be deleted wholesale. Migration never modified the legacy state directory, so no user directory has to be cleaned up; copied targets and .pre-migration backups stay for the user to keep or remove.
